title: Fully physics-driven player movemen
author: emolist
selftext:
Hello, guys, some time in the past I started to work on game I envisioned, and found out there are no REAL physics-controlled movement, like in Exanima for example, or similar to what used in GTA V. So I decided to make one for myself. In the process of creation I had a thought "What if someone else is having the same problem in finding something like that?". And that's what I want to ask you. Is there anyone else who need their 3d person to move entirely by physics engine or is it just me? Please let me know if you're interested in this type of thing. Thanks. 

P.S. By the way, if I made any mistakes in spelling words, please don't be mad, English is not my first language.

comments.author: Lotton
comments.body: Are you talking about a ragdoll effect?

comments.author: Xylozene
comments.body: Can you explain what "Fully physics driven player movement" actually means to you? Becuase I've been programming physics for nearly 10 years and I am having hard time understanding what fully physics driven movement actually is? Do you mean no animations and all movement is completely procedural? Animating without bones? Or do you mean a proper skeleton, with muscles that drive movement through What do you actually mean?

replies.author: Neither-Upstairs
replies.body: They used GTA5 as an example which makes me think that they really don’t know what they’re talking about lmao

comments.author: Neither-Upstairs
comments.body: Yeah this is not new territory, games like human fall flat and gang beasts are 3rd person perspective games with player controllers entirely driven by physics. I’m working on something similar.

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body: I think your AI has misled you. You are probably working without a 3d engine and what your AI means is that it hasn't implemented it in whatever tech stack you're using. Either tell it to implement it, or use an engine like Unity, Unreal, or Godot.

comments.author: Valentinevandal1986
comments.body: So I am actually working on something, if what you’re talking about is the same thing. I’m basically working on a system I call “Pathfire” that I don’t really want to get into the specifics of but it’s essentially a “smart” navigation system that will be blending a few open source technologies for a traversal system that I’ve personally never seen (and maybe with good reason) but I’m going to try it
